title_en: Chen Xingliang v. Digital Library — copyright infringement dispute

full_text_en:
Chen Xingliang v. China Digital Library Co., Ltd. — dispute over copyright infringement

Plaintiff: Chen Xingliang, male, 45 years old, professor at Peking University Law School, residing in Haidian District, Beijing.

Defendant: China Digital Library Co., Ltd. Domicile: Haidian District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Zhang Yanbo, Chairman of the Company.

Plaintiff Chen Xingliang filed a lawsuit with the Haidian District People's Court of Beijing against Defendant China Digital Library Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Digital Library") for copyright infringement.

Plaintiff's Allegations: The Defendant, without the Plaintiff's consent, used three of the Plaintiff's works on its website (URL: http://www.d-library.com.cn). After paying a fee, readers become members of the Defendant's website and can read and download the online works. This conduct by the Defendant infringed on the Plaintiff's right to network dissemination of information. The Plaintiff requests the court to order the Defendant to immediately cease the infringement and to compensate the Plaintiff for economic losses of RMB 400,000, as well as reasonable expenses of RMB 8,000 incurred by the Plaintiff in stopping the Defendant's infringing acts.

The Plaintiff submitted four pieces of evidence: 1. Copies of the copyright pages of the three works; 2. Notarized certificates and reading cards; 3. Reading card receipts; 4. Invoices.

Defendant's Defense: The Defendant is essentially a public welfare-oriented institution. To meet the needs of the general public in the information age, the Defendant established the "China Digital Library" online. The nature of a library is to collect various books for public reading and reference. The three works referred to by the Plaintiff have all been publicly published and distributed. Including them in the Digital Library is conducive to the secondary development and utilization of these works and should not be considered infringement. Moreover, the Defendant has always attached great importance to copyright protection and is currently investing funds in developing a copyright protection system. Once this system is developed, it will, on one hand, protect the interests of copyright holders from infringement, and on the other hand, enable the Digital Library to better serve the public. The Defendant requests the court to adjudicate this dispute based on the current actual situation of the "China Digital Library" and in light of China's national conditions.

The Defendant submitted four pieces of evidence: 1. Official letter from the Ministry of Culture regarding the application for the establishment of "China Digital Library Co., Ltd."; 2. Request for prefixing "China Digital Library Co., Ltd." with the word "China"; 3. Official instruction regarding prefixing "China Digital Library Co., Ltd." with the word "China"; 4. Notice from the State Development Planning Commission regarding the approval of the Digital Library project.

The Haidian District People's Court of Beijing, upon trial, confirmed the following facts:

1. *New Perspectives on Contemporary Chinese Criminal Law* was first published in April 1999 by China University of Political Science and Law Press. The book contains 754,000 characters, with a print run of 3,000 copies, priced at RMB 45. *General Theory of Criminal Law Application* was first published in June 1999 by Law Press. The book contains 1,170,000 characters, with a print run of 5,000 copies, priced at RMB 96. *On Self-Defense* was first published in June 1987 by Renmin University of China Press. The book contains 206,000 characters, with a print run of 10,000 copies, priced at RMB 1.7. Plaintiff Chen Xingliang is the author of these three books. Evidence 1 submitted by the Plaintiff can prove the above facts.

2. The Defendant Digital Library was established on January 17, 2000, with the enterprise nature of a limited liability company. Its business scope includes technical development of computer software, technology transfer, e-commerce (excluding projects requiring special permits), and production and posting of online advertisements. On March 11, 2002, the company underwent annual industrial and commercial inspection and registration. The "China Digital Library" website operated by the company mainly collects, organizes, and publishes others' works. Evidence 1 to 4 and the business license submitted by Digital Library can prove the above facts.

3. The access method for the "China Digital Library" website is as follows: using a networked host, launch IE browser version 5.5, type www.d-library.com.cn in the address bar, and enter the homepage of "China Digital Library." The homepage notes "Copyright: China Digital Library Co., Ltd."; clicking "Download Standard Browser" on that page, a new page displays "China Digital Library Browser Beta 1.01 is a dedicated browser developed by China Digital Library Co., Ltd. for online libraries. Readers can conveniently enter the online library to read and borrow books without leaving home, and at the same time, copyright protection is implemented online in a unique way." It also prompts: "Readers need to apply for a reading card to browse and borrow books—pay by online or card method, and obtain a username and password through user registration." The notarized certificate in Evidence 2 submitted by Plaintiff Chen Xingliang can prove the above facts.

4. On the homepage of the "China Digital Library" website, using the "Advanced Search" system, entering "Chen Xingliang" as the search term, and "Responsible Person" as the search path, the search results include the three works involved in this case: *New Perspectives on Contemporary Chinese Criminal Law*, *General Theory of Criminal Law Application*, and *On Self-Defense*, along with relevant information about these three works. For example, the information about *New Perspectives on Contemporary Chinese Criminal Law* includes: Title and Responsible Person: "*New Perspectives on Contemporary Chinese Criminal Law* by Chen Xingliang"; Publisher: "Beijing: China University of Political Science and Law Press, 1999"; Physical Form: "897 pages; 20cm"; Subject Term: "Criminal Law - Research - China", etc. The notarized certificate in Evidence 2 submitted by Plaintiff Chen Xingliang can prove the above facts.

5. In March 2002, a third party, Zhang Qingfang, registered as a user of the "China Digital Library" under the username "Zhang Dai" and ID number 370602730301353, with an interest in legal books, etc., and was assigned registration number 459757, valid from March 13, 2002, to June 11, 2002. On March 15, 2002, Zhang Qingfang used his registration number to read the three works involved in this case on the "China Digital Library" website and printed some pages on-site. Evidence 2 and 3 submitted by Plaintiff Chen Xingliang can prove the above facts.

6. In connection with this lawsuit, Plaintiff Chen Xingliang paid attorney fees of RMB 8,000, which Chen Xingliang claims as reasonable expenses incurred to stop the infringing acts. Evidence 4 submitted by Chen Xingliang can prove the above facts.

The above facts are also confirmed by the trial transcript.

The Haidian District People's Court of Beijing held:

First, Article 2 of the Copyright Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Copyright Law) provides: "Works of Chinese citizens, legal persons, or other organizations, whether published or not, shall enjoy copyright in accordance with this Law." Article 11(1) provides: "Copyright belongs to the author, except as otherwise provided in this Law." Paragraph (2) provides: "The citizen who creates the work is the author." Pursuant to Article 10(1)(12) of the Copyright Law, copyright includes "the right of network dissemination of information," that is, the right to provide works to the public by wire or wireless means, so that the public may obtain the works from information networks at a time and place individually chosen.

Copyright is an exclusive right granted to authors by law, and authors have the right to restrict others from using their works without permission. Such restriction can only be exercised by the author when the public's access to the work expands to an extent that may affect the author's exercise of copyright. Plaintiff Chen Xingliang legally enjoys the copyright in the three works *New Perspectives on Contemporary Chinese Criminal Law*, *General Theory of Criminal Law Application*, and *On Self-Defense*, and has the right to license others to use his works. In the absence of contrary evidence, it can only be determined at present that Chen Xingliang allowed the relevant publishing houses to fix these three works on paper and provide them to the public by means of publication and distribution. The Defendant Digital Library, without Chen Xingliang's permission, included these three works on the "China Digital Library" website, which inevitably affects Chen Xingliang's exercise of copyright in these works in cyberspace and infringes on Chen Xingliang's right to network dissemination of information in his works.

Article 47(1) of the Copyright Law provides that without the permission of the copyright owner, "reproducing, distributing, performing, broadcasting, displaying, compiling, or disseminating their works to the public through information networks" constitutes infringement, and the infringer "shall, according to the circumstances, bear civil liability such as cessation of infringement, elimination of effects, apology, and compensation for losses." The Defendant Digital Library shall bear civil liability for infringement in accordance with the law.

Second, a library is an institution that collects, organizes, and stores books and materials for public reading and reference. Its function is to preserve works and provide the public with opportunities to access works. Libraries providing works to the public are of great significance for disseminating knowledge and promoting social civilization and progress. Only specific members of the public (readers eligible for reading) can access the works provided by the library at specific times and in specific ways (borrowing). Therefore, such access has a limited impact on the author's exercise of copyright and does not constitute infringement.

The Defendant Digital Library, as a corporate legal person, uploaded the Plaintiff Chen Xingliang's works onto the Internet. This method of using the works expands the time and space of dissemination of the works, increases the number of people who can access the works, and exceeds the scope within which the author allows the public to access his works. The Digital Library used Chen Xingliang's works online without permission and failed to take effective measures to ensure that Chen Xingliang received reasonable compensation. This conduct impedes Chen Xingliang's lawful exercise of copyright in his works and constitutes infringement. The Digital Library's defense denying infringement is unfounded.

Third, Article 64(1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "A party has the responsibility to provide evidence for its claims." Article 48(1) of the Copyright Law provides: "Where copyright or copyright-related rights are infringed, the infringer shall compensate based on the actual losses of the right holder; if the actual losses are difficult to calculate, compensation may be based on the illegal gains of the infringer. The amount of compensation shall also include the reasonable expenses paid by the right holder to stop the infringing act." Paragraph (2) provides: "If the actual losses of the right holder or the illegal gains of the infringer cannot be determined, the people's court shall, based on the circumstances of the infringement, award compensation of not more than RMB 500,000." Plaintiff Chen Xingliang claims that the Defendant Digital Library's infringement caused him economic losses of RMB 400,000 and incurred attorney fees of RMB 8,000, and requests compensation. However, Chen Xingliang did not provide evidence to prove that his actual losses or the infringer's illegal gains are equivalent to the amount claimed, nor did he demonstrate the reasonableness of the RMB 8,000 attorney fees. Therefore, the amount of compensation from the Digital Library can only be determined based on the circumstances of the infringement, and the full amount of Chen Xingliang's claimed compensation cannot be granted.

Accordingly, the Haidian District People's Court of Beijing, on June 27, 2002, rendered the following judgment:

(1) From the date this judgment takes effect, the Defendant Digital Library shall cease using the Plaintiff Chen Xingliang's works *New Perspectives on Contemporary Chinese Criminal Law*, *General Theory of Criminal Law Application*, and *On Self-Defense* on its "China Digital Library" website;

(2) Within 10 days from the date this judgment takes effect, the Defendant Digital Library shall compensate Plaintiff Chen Xingliang for economic losses of RMB 80,000 and reasonable litigation expenses of RMB 4,800;

(3) Reject Plaintiff Chen Xingliang's other claims.

Court acceptance fee: RMB 8,660, to be borne by the Defendant Digital Library.

After the judgment was announced, neither party appealed.
